mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Certificate of Registration of Foreign-Invested Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry or State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) of PRC, as applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization before the notary public of the place of issue, then apostille by the competent central authority if the issuing jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille Convention member state; if the issuing jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention member, replace apostille with consular legalization processed through the foreign ministry and the consular post of the receiving state. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel, mutually exclusive paths and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Current Status
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry for HK entities or SAMR Enterprise Credit Information Report for the PRC FIP limb
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original certificate notarized by a local notary, then authenticated either by apostille under the Hague Apostille Convention or by consular legalization for non-member states; the two chains are alternative only, and no mixed or cumulative authentication is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Partners' Resolution or Board Resolution appointing the first registered agent, authorized representatives, and approving the SPAC acquisition mandate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding partners or directors of the formation entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execution before the notary public of the country of execution, followed by apostille (Hague member states) or consular legalization (non-member states), elected as a single route based on the destination state's membership status.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Partnership Agreement including capital commitments, UBO waterfall provisions and AML representations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founders and their counsel, certified by a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the agreement, then apostille by the designated Hague Convention competent authority, or consular legalization via the competent embassy/consulate if the source jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention signatory; the two methods are mutually exclusive and sequential use is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the initial equity provider or financing bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank maintaining the account-holder relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank-letterhead reference, notarized when required, then delivered either with apostille (Hague) or consular legalization (non-Hague), or directly through bank-to-bank authenticated channels if recognized; for all official filing bundles the apostille path must not be combined with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration and Significant Controllers Register extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Designated representative or company secretary of the entity, verified by a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the UBO declaration and register extract followed by apostille if the execution state is a Hague member; if not, consular legalization is the exclusive alternative. No sequential or combined authentication chain is acceptable.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based due diligence requires positive-identification screening of all partners, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, authorized signatories, sponsors and counterparties against (i) HK Monetary Authority sanctioned and politically exposed persons lists, (ii) the Hong Kong Commerce and Economic Development Bureau consolidated sanctions list, (iii) UN Security Council consolidated lists, (iv) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, (v) PRC Ministry of Public Security sanctions and wanted lists, and (vi) adverse-media, enforcement and regulatory action databases. Screening must be refreshed at least quarterly and on any trigger event, with false-positive disposal fully documented; source of wealth and source of funds for every UBO above the 25% threshold must be supported by independent documentary evidence retained for not less than five years; positive PEP matches require senior management escalation, enhanced due diligence, and risk approval before any incorporation step, bank onboarding, or trust escrow instruction is executed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) and, for the PRC FIP limb, the SAMR National Enterprise Registration and Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Hong Kong permits one English name and one traditional Chinese name for a registered foreign entity or company. The English name must not be identical to a name appearing on the Companies Registry Index; the Chinese name, if adopted, must be composed of Traditional Chinese characters and must comply with the Phonetic or Semantic Transliteration Doctrine. For the PRC Foreign-Invested Partnership, the Administrative Provisions on Enterprise Name Registration impose a four-tier naming structure: administrative division + distinctive name + industry or business characterization (e.g., 'Special Purpose Acquisition' or 'Investment') + organizational form ('Foreign-Invested Partnership'). Any English-HK/PRC transliteration must preserve the core distinctive element and must not materially differ in pronunciation or meaning from the approved registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the proposed name, the applicant may request internal reconsideration from the Hong Kong Companies Registry within 14 days of the rejection notice by filing the prescribed review application together with the original rejection, revised name alternatives, a statutory declaration confirming non-collision, and, where a sensitive token caused rejection, the prior written waiver or consent of the relevant licensing authority. The Registry is obligated to issue a written ruling within 21 business days. If the rejection is sustained, the applicant may appeal to the Administrative Appeals Board within 60 days of the ruling, and ultimately seek judicial review before the Court of First Instance. For the PRC FIP limb, the applicant should file administrative reconsideration with the SAMR at the next higher level within 60 days of the rejection, attaching evidence of prior use of the mark and any pre-approval letters for prohibited tokens, followed by administrative litigation before the People's Court if reconsideration is unsuccessful. The entire appeal process must be documented in English and Chinese where required by the receiving authority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not absolutely prohibited for Hong Kong registered office purposes, but it is operationally unacceptable for this SPAC-class entity. The Inland Revenue Department, HKMA, and licensed banks will typically reject a pure virtual address for a blank-check entity because it lacks demonstrable physical substance, management presence, and adequate records-keeping capacity. For the mainland PRC FIP, SAMR and PBOC require a fixed, non-residential registered address capable of receiving official correspondence and permitting unannounced inspection; a commercial mailbox without lease or staffing fails this test. Accordingly, a physical Hong Kong office, even if small or in a serviced-office building, is mandatory for bank onboarding, trust escrow arrangements, and any public-market listing preparation; virtual office solutions may only serve as an auxiliary back-office and cannot be the sole registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced on-site inspection likelihood is quantified as HIGH (>65%) where the registered address is a virtual or serviced mailbox and the entity claims SPAC or acquisition activity, and MODERATE (30-50%) for a serviced office where no dedicated employee is present during business hours. Municipal tax authorities, SAMR, and the Companies Registry may conduct inspections of site accessibility, lease documents, physical signage, employee presence, office equipment, and records storage. Inspection triggers include: (i) absent lease in the entity name; (ii) no staff or human response at the registered address; (iii) mail forwarding exclusively to a corporate services provider; (iv) high-risk industry classification; (v) UBO register showing no local manager or director; (vi) inconsistencies between tax filings, bank statements, and declared business scope; and (vii) use of a mass-registration address. One adverse inspection can result in removal from the register, cancellation of the certificate of good standing, or refusal by a bank to open or maintain the escrow/trust account.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37) of the Laws of Hong Kong, particularly sections 4 (constitution of limited partnership), 5 (registration), and 6 (requirements for registration). Also applicable provisions of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) if the general partner is a company.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP1 (Application for Registration of Limited Partnership) and Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Hong Kong limited partnerships have no minimum capital requirement. However, the partnership agreement must specify capital contributions. For SPAC purposes, the listing rules require a trust account to hold IPO proceeds, but this is not a statutory capital requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER AND LIMITED PARTNERS OF [PARTNERSHIP NAME] (THE 'PARTNERSHIP') ADOPTED AT WRITING ON [DATE] PURSUANT TO THE PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT AND THE LIMITED PARTNERSHIP ORDINANCE (CAP. 37) OF THE LAWS OF HONG KONG.

WHEREAS the Partnership has been formed as a limited partnership for the purpose of conducting a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) business, and the Partners desire to adopt the initial governance and operational resolutions.

NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The capital contributions of the Partners as set forth in the Partnership Agreement are hereby ratified and confirmed. The General Partner is authorized to call upon and receive such contributions in accordance with the terms of the Partnership Agreement. The total capital contributions shall be deposited into the designated bank account as set forth in Resolution 3.

2. APPOINTMENT OF GENERAL PARTNER: [Name of General Partner] is hereby appointed as the General Partner of the Partnership, with full authority to manage the affairs of the Partnership, subject to the sole discretion and limitations set forth in the Partnership Agreement and applicable law. The General Partner shall have the power to execute documents, enter into contracts, and take all actions necessary to carry out the Partnership's business.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Partnership shall open and maintain a bank account with [Bank Name] (the 'Bank'). The General Partner is hereby authorized to execute all account opening documents, designate authorized signatories, and give instructions to the Bank regarding the operation of the account, including but not limited to wire transfers, deposits, and withdrawals. The authorized signatories shall be [Name of Signatory 1] and [Name of Signatory 2], and any two of them shall sign jointly for any transaction exceeding [Amount].

4. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The registered office of the Partnership shall be at [Address] in Hong Kong. The General Partner is authorized to file all necessary documents with the Companies Registry to establish such address as the registered office.

5. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: [Name] is appointed as the Compliance Officer, [Name] as the Money Laundering Reporting Officer, and [Name] as the Company Secretary (if applicable) of the Partnership, each to serve until removed or replaced by the General Partner. The officers shall have the duties and responsibilities as prescribed by the Partnership Agreement and applicable law.

6. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The General Partner and each officer are hereby authorized to take all such steps, execute all necessary documents, and incur all such expenses as may be necessary or desirable to implement the foregoing resolutions and to comply with all applicable laws and regulations.

This resolution is effective as of the date first written above and shall remain in force until revoked or amended by a subsequent resolution of the Partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry (for name check) and Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the Companies Registry's online system to ensure the proposed partnership name is not identical to an existing company or partnership. If the name is available, proceed to apply for a Business Registration Certificate from the Business Registration Office within one month of commencement of business. The application must include the partnership name, nature of business, and registered address. Provide the required fee and supporting documents. The Business Registration Office will issue a certificate upon successful processing. This step is essential to legally operate the partnership in Hong Kong.
required_dossiers: Business description and registered office address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, select an alternative name and resubmit. If the Business Registration application is queried, provide additional information or address the query within the specified deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Hong Kong law firm to draft a comprehensive partnership agreement that complies with the Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37) and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) requirements for SPACs. The agreement must specify capital contributions, profit and loss sharing, management structure, dissolution rights, and the role of the general partner. All partners must review and execute the agreement. The executed agreement is a foundational document for registration and banking. Ensure the agreement addresses the SPAC's trust account and IPO proceeds handling.
required_dossiers: Proof of address for each partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the agreement is incomplete or non-compliant, legal counsel will revise and circulate for re-execution. Any partner disputes must be resolved before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Form LP1 (Application for Registration of Limited Partnership) along with the executed partnership agreement and the prescribed fee to the Companies Registry. The form must be signed by the general partner. The Registry will review the application for compliance with the Limited Partnership Ordinance. Upon approval, the Registry will issue a Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership. Ensure all details are accurate and consistent with the partnership agreement to avoid rejection.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the Registry's queries within the specified period, provide additional documents, or amend the partnership agreement as required. If rejected, correct the deficiencies and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Business Registration Certificate and Open Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office (for BR) and licensed banks (for account opening)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Registration, apply for a Business Registration Certificate from the Business Registration Office if not already obtained. This certificate is mandatory for all businesses. Then, open a corporate bank account with a licensed bank in Hong Kong. For a SPAC, a trust account must be established to hold IPO proceeds. Provide the bank with the partnership's registration documents, partnership agreement, and KYC documents. The bank will conduct due diligence and may require additional information. Ensure compliance with anti-money laundering regulations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
KYC documents (passport, proof of address, source of funds)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Registration is delayed, follow up with the office. If the bank account application is rejected, provide additional documentation or choose an alternative bank. For the trust account, ensure compliance with SFC requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Inland Revenue Department (IRD) with online eTAX portal; for People's Republic of China mainland tax nexus, the State Taxation Administration (STA) with provincial electronic tax declaration portals.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Confirm whether the Foreign-Invested Partnership carries on business in Hong Kong. Step 2: Within one month of commencing business, submit the statutory Business Registration application to the Business Registration Office of the Hong Kong IRD, using the eTAX portal or paper channels, together with the partnership agreement, partner identification documents, registered address proof, and any authorization to an appointed agent. Step 3: After processing, the IRD issues a Business Registration Certificate and Business Registration Number (BRN) which serves as the Hong Kong taxpayer identifier. Step 4: If a permanent establishment or fixed place of business is created in mainland China, register with the competent STA tax bureau within 30 days of establishment via the electronic tax registration procedure, providing the unified social credit code certificate or equivalent, the partnership registration certificate, the partnership agreement, bank account opening permit or notice, and the authorized person's identity documents. Step 5: The STA will issue a statutory taxpayer identification number (TIN) and classify the partnership for VAT purposes; the same TIN is used for enterprise income tax filings, VAT filings, and withholding filings. Step 6: Any separate registration with the Hong Kong Companies Registry is not a substitute for the IRD Business Registration, and any PRC market registration must be followed by the STA tax registration before the partnership can lawfully issue invoices in mainland China.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the Foreign-Invested Partnership is a fiscally transparent partnership for Hong Kong Profits Tax and PRC enterprise income tax on partnerships. Profits are assessable in the hands of the partners. The Hong Kong territorial source principle limits taxability to profits arising in or derived from Hong Kong, while PRC source rules apply to income derived from mainland China. The entity is not eligible for corporate-style entity-level taxation unless a separate corporate wrapper is interposed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Hong Kong does not provide a check-the-box election, and the PRC tax system requires partnerships to be treated as flow-through entities for enterprise income tax. Individual partners may elect personal assessment under the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Ordinance to aggregate salaries, profits and property income for progressive tax relief, but this is not a classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: PRC Value-Added Tax (VAT) is the applicable indirect tax where a mainland China taxable supply or permanent establishment exists; Hong Kong itself has no VAT, GST or general sales tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mainland China: VAT registration is immediate upon commencement of taxable activities; mandatory general VAT taxpayer status is triggered when annual taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000 (small-scale taxpayer threshold). Hong Kong: no VAT registration threshold, but a Business Registration Certificate is required on commencement of business regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mainland China operates the State Taxation Administration's Golden Tax System IV (full digital electronic invoices and fiscal clearance). VAT invoices must be created and reported online in near real time, with anti-counterfeit stamping, automatic data filing to the STA, and strict invoice inventory control. Hong Kong has no VAT fiscal clearance, no real-time e-invoicing mandate, and no digital stamping requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under PRC VAT law, zero-rating applies to genuine cross-border exports of goods where the exporter is a general VAT taxpayer registered for export tax refunds, the goods are physically declared to Chinese customs for export, the export invoice matches the customs declaration, logistics documents and payment, and foreign exchange is received or legally repatriated. Qualifying cross-border services listed by the Ministry of Finance and STA may also be zero-rated or VAT-exempt. For Hong Kong, no VAT is levied, so exports are outside the scope of indirect tax and no zero-rating filing is made to the IRD.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) issued by the PRC Customs (Customs Export Goods Declaration)

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Bank of China (PBOC) for sovereign mainland China cross-border RMB and FX approval matters; Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as the de facto central bank and banking regulator for the Hong Kong SAR's offshore CNH clearing and U.S. dollar interbank settlement infrastructure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Hong Kong operates a fully convertible currency regime under the HKMA's currency board system, with the Hong Kong dollar pegged to the U.S. dollar in a 7.75-7.85 band. There are no surrender requirements, capital account controls, or profit repatriation restrictions in Hong Kong. Mainland China, however, maintains a managed floating exchange rate regime with a two-tier convertibility structure: the RMB is fully convertible for current account transactions (trade in goods and services, dividends, interest) upon submission of supporting documents, but capital account transactions, including outbound direct investment, portfolio flows, and cross-border financing, require prior approval or registration with SAFE. For a China-based Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) seeking to inject capital into an HK SPAC vehicle, the outbound investment must be recorded under the Outbound Direct Investment (ODI) framework or through qualified outbound investor schemes (QDLP/QDIE). Profit remittances from the HK SPAC back to mainland FIP partners are subject to Chinese foreign exchange registration, tax filing with the State Taxation Administration, and verification of the genuine nature of the funds. Onshore CNY remains restricted, while offshore CNH is freely traded in Hong Kong; the two are distinct and cannot be fungible without a dedicated regulatory gateway. All treasury operations must therefore maintain strict separation between onshore CNY settlement and offshore CNH/USD/HKD flows to avoid inadvertent creation of an unregulated cross-border channel.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For the Mainland China operating segment, SAFE mandates that export proceeds in foreign currency must be repatriated into a domestic foreign exchange settlement account within 90 days of the customs export declaration, and 100% of such proceeds must be surrendered or settled into RMB unless the exporter is licensed to retain FX under a valid exemption. Advance export receipts must be swept into the designated account within 30 days of collection. In contrast, the Hong Kong SAR, as the offshore special territory, imposes no surrender rules; all foreign currency receipts may be retained indefinitely and deployed freely across the escrow and operational treasury frameworks without mandatory conversion or repatriation deadlines.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for SPAC treasury use. Licensed digital EMI platforms operating in Hong Kong under the HKMA's Stored Value Facility and Money Service Operator regimes are legally prohibited from holding client trust money for escrow-based blank-check acquisition vehicles. Their terms of service typically exclude corporate escrow duties, and their AML/CTF systems are not calibrated to the complex multi-party partnership structures, inbound mainland capital, and unknown target exposure intrinsic to an SPAC. While such EMIs may provide ancillary payroll or expense accounts, any attempt to use them for capital injection routing, trust escrow, or acquisition consideration clearing will be rejected by the HKMA as a breach of the Banking Ordinance and AMLO. A licensed Tier-1 commercial bank with a dedicated SPAC practice is the only acceptable route.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors, general partners, and all ultimate beneficial owners holding 10% or more of the Foreign-Invested Partnership must undergo an in-branch KYC interview at the chosen Hong Kong bank's corporate banking centre. Remote opening via televised video call is permitted only if the natural person is physically present in a jurisdiction approved by the HKMA, and the interview is conducted through the bank's secure video conferencing platform while the individual submits wet-ink notarized identification documents to the bank's local correspondent within 14 days. A consular proxy cannot fully substitute for the statutory director's personal interview during the formation stage. If any partner is an offshore company, that entity's directors must provide a Board Resolution authenticated by a Hong Kong CPA, and the ultimate individual owners must still complete the in-person or video KYC interview before the account can be activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Blank-check SPAC structure with no operating business and ISIC 6499 classification (other financial service activities) creates elevated risk of layering via escrowed third-party funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive source-of-wealth report for each capital contributor including notarized partnership agreements, audited personal/corporate bank statements for the past 12 months, tax clearance certificates from mainland China and Hong Kong, a fully executed trust/escrow agreement appointing a licensed custodian, and a detailed SPAC white paper outlining target acquisition sectors and a transparent timeline for the release of escrowed funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) chain traverses mainland China into a Hong Kong partnership, with pass-through taxation and a multi-level ownership register, causing opacity and potential nominee/shareholder concealment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified register of members from the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) for the PRC partners, Hong Kong Companies Registry Certificate of Registration for any Part X non-HK entity, notarized copies of all UBO passports or HKID cards, a complete ownership tree chart demonstrating every layer, sworn declarations that no bearer shares or nominee structures exist, and a legal opinion from a licensed PRC and Hong Kong law firm validating the partnership's standing and the ultimate individual owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow funds are destined for a future public market acquisition where the target is unknown, exposing the bank to sanctions and politically exposed persons (PEP) risk without a prior transaction pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An undertaking executed by the general partner that no acquisition target shall be a sanctions-listed or PEP-affiliated entity, pre-signed declarations of no PEP affiliation for all partners and their immediate family members, a subscription agreement detailing each investor's source of funds, and a contractual commitment to provide the final target's full KYC and AML screening pack to the bank at least 30 days prior to any escrowed fund release.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injections from multiple mainland Chinese investors routed via SAFE-registered ODI create potential cross-border wire fragmentation and unexplained circular payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Itemized capital account mapping tying each SAFE ODI registration code to the corresponding wire instruction and ultimate source enterprise, NDRC outbound investment certificates, notarized board resolutions from the FIP's general partner, a written explanation of the economic rationale for each incoming transfer, and an independent audit engagement letter from a Big Four firm to verify escrow account movements quarterly.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital from mainland China into the HK SPAC escrow account must be routed via SWIFT MT103/202 with strict reference to SAFE purpose code 227012 (Overseas Investment in Securities / Special Purpose Vehicle) and the approved ODI registration number. The Chinese FIP shall convert CNY to HKD/USD through a designated onshore bank, submit the SAFE settlement memorandum and capital verification report, and remit the funds as a cross-border payment under the RMB/CNH clearing bridge between BOCHK onshore and the Hong Kong arm. Upon arrival, the HK bank receives the funds into the Escrow Trust Account, and a Hong Kong certified public accountant performs capital verification against the FIP subscription agreement and the SAFE notification of receipt. For non-mainland contributors, inbound wires must include the source denomination and a beneficiary legal entity identifier matching the FIP's HK registration, and the bank's compliance team will quarantine the funds until the source-of-wealth dossier is validated.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operational trade settlement, the HK SPAC uses SWIFT MT103 direct payments for services, professional fees, and minor purchase obligations. For acquisition-related disbursements, the escrow account clears via CHATS (Clearing House Automated Transfer System) for HK-listed stock settlement and via Fedwire/CHIPS for US/global targets. Where the acquisition involves physical goods or documentary trade, a Commercial Letter of Credit at sight or a Documentary Collection (D/P or D/A) will be routed through the issuing HK bank using UCP600/URC522 rules. All outbound disbursements from the escrow account must be supported by a director-approved release memorandum, a signed target acquisition agreement, and a compliance sign-off confirming that no sanctioned counterparty is involved.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts with a licensed Hong Kong bank for fixing HKD/USD or CNH/USD conversion rates on known escrow release dates.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on the offshore CNH market for hedging RMB exposure of the mainland FIP partners, transacted through HKMA-authorized counterparties only.
Cross-currency swaps between HKD and CNH or CNY for liquidity matching when the partnership holds multi-currency capital commitments and needs to align asset and liability durations.

Currency options (vanilla put/call) to protect the escrow account value against adverse USD/CNH moves, provided the options are physically settled through the HK clearing house and not cash-settled outside regulatory oversight.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate renewal and prescribed levy
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Business Registration Office, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the expiry date shown on the current one-year Business Registration Certificate, being the business registration anniversary date; renewal is required annually.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew by the expiry date may attract a late surcharge of HKD 300, a fine of up to HKD 5,000, and imprisonment for up to one year; continuing default will cause the IRD registration record to become inactive and may expose every responsible partner to prosecution and administrative deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return for the partnership (form BIR52) together with supporting profit and loss account, balance sheet, and tax computations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the issue date shown on the BIR52; where a Hong Kong tax representative is appointed and the financial statements are drawn to 31 March, the IRD block extension arrangement normally extends the due date for partnerships to mid-August or early November, but the statutory deadline specified in the return always controls.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is an offence under section 80 of the Inland Revenue Ordinance, punishable by a fine of up to HKD 10,000 and a daily fine of HKD 1,000; the assessor may raise an estimated assessment under section 59(3), impose additional tax of up to 100 percent for incorrect returns, and add a threefold penalty on unpaid tax; administrative collection measures may follow against partnership assets and partner property.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of remuneration and pensions (BIR56A and IR56B forms) for every Hong Kong employee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the due date specified by the IRD, normally by 30 April for the year of assessment ending 31 March immediately preceding.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the employer's return may attract a fine of up to HKD 10,000 and a daily default fine of HKD 1,000; the IRD may estimate remuneration, disallow compensation deductions, and prosecute each responsible partner or director.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return or annual information statement for the Foreign-Invested Partnership where it is registered as a Limited Partnership Fund under the Limited Partnership Funds Ordinance, Cap 637
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry, Limited Partnership Funds Unit, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of the date of registration of the Limited Partnership Fund in the Companies Registry.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is an offence under the Limited Partnership Funds Ordinance; the partnership and each general partner may be liable to a fine at Level 3, currently up to HKD 10,000, plus a daily default fine; repetitive default may cause the Companies Registry to commence administrative deregistration or strike-off action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Companies Registry Annual Return (form NAR1) for any Hong Kong incorporated corporate general partner or corporate SPAC holding entity in the group
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of the incorporation date of the corporate entity.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts escalating late fees from HKD 520 where default is not more than 3 months up to HKD 3,120 where default exceeds 9 months; prosecution may result in a fine of up to HKD 50,000 and a daily fine of HKD 1,000; persistent default for more than 6 months may trigger strike-off by the Registrar under section 746 of the Companies Ordinance with vesting of assets in the Government of the Hong Kong SAR.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Securities and Futures Commission licence fee renewal and annual AML/CFT compliance confirmation for the SPAC sponsor or investment manager
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the expiry date of the SFC licence, being the anniversary of the original licence issue; the annual AML/CFT confirmation and beneficial ownership refresh are required within 30 days after the corporate financial year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment or failure to renew may result in licence suspension and SFC disciplinary sanctions; carrying on regulated activity without a valid licence is a criminal offence under the Securities and Futures Ordinance, Cap 571, punishable by fine and imprisonment; the SFC may suspend or revoke the licence, publicly reprimand responsible officers, and impose enforceable pecuniary penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Publication and filing of audited annual results, annual report, and periodic disclosure documents for the SPAC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited (HKEX) Listing Division and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual results must be published within 3 months after the financial year end and the annual report must be dispatched within 4 months after the financial year end, in accordance with the HKEX Listing Rules; the exact anniversary rule also requires continued compliance with the annual financial disclosure calendar of the SPAC.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to publish annual results within the prescribed period will normally cause an immediate trading suspension; continued non-compliance allows HKEX to impose a fine, issue a directive, and ultimately cancel the SPAC listing; the SFC may separately take enforcement action under the Securities and Futures Ordinance, including disciplinary fines, public censure, and disqualification of responsible persons.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Hong Kong imposes no size-based audit exemption for an incorporated SPAC or a licensed financial entity; therefore the quantitative threshold is effectively zero. Audit is compulsory from the first accounting period regardless of balance sheet size, turnover, or headcount if the vehicle or any of its general partners is incorporated under the Companies Ordinance, Cap 622, in which case a practising certified public accountant must be appointed under sections 405 and 411 and audited financial statements must be laid before the annual general meeting within 9 months of the financial year end. If the Foreign-Invested Partnership is an unincorporated Limited Partnership Fund under Cap 637, audit becomes compulsory when the partnership agreement, the SFC licence condition, or an HKEX requirement mandates it; in practice a SPAC sponsor and investment manager licensed by the SFC must submit audited annual financial statements under the SFC Code of Conduct and the Securities and Futures (Financial Resources) Rules irrespective of size. The HKEX SPAC regime requires public accountability, so the vehicle cannot use the HKFRS for Private Entities framework; it must prepare financial statements under HKFRS or IFRS and the auditor must apply Hong Kong Standards on Auditing. No headcount or revenue threshold can exempt the SPAC or its licensed manager from audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) for Hong Kong incorporated entities; IFRS as issued by the IASB for foreign incorporated SPAC holding vehicles; HKEX Listing Rules financial disclosure standards; Hong Kong Standards on Auditing issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants; and, for SFC licensed corporations, the SFC financial resources and accounting records requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong has no central public annual UBO filing for partnerships, but the SPAC structure must maintain robust beneficial ownership records. The general partner and responsible person must keep a Significant Controllers Register at the registered office where a corporate entity is part of the structure, and update it within 15 days of any change. For a Limited Partnership Fund, any change to the general partner, responsible person, registered office, or registered details must be notified to the Companies Registry within 15 days. The SFC and HKEX must be notified of any transfer of beneficial ownership, sponsor equity, or partnership interest equal to or exceeding 10 percent within 30 days of the transfer. As a Medium-Risk Enhanced AML entity, the SPAC sponsor must conduct an annual refresh of beneficial ownership information and file the annual AML/CFT confirmation with the SFC within 30 days after the corporate year end.
